lines.text: Welcome back to Beau's Slow English.
Today, I'm going to talk about
hairstyles for men and women. I used to
be a hair stylist for 10 years, and I
was thinking there's a lot of vocabulary
that could be useful for you. When I was
a hair stylist, I worked in a hair
salon.
[clears throat]
I received my cosmetology license when I
was 19 years old. In America, if you
would like to be a hair stylist, you
have to attend cosmetology school.
Cosmetology is the study of hair, skin,
and nails. Although I studied
hair, skin, and nails, I chose to
specialize
in hair. After you complete all of your
hours that is required by the state, you
can then take the state board exam. This
exam was extremely
scary. It made me very anxious, but I
passed, and I received my license. I
received my first license in the state
of Maryland,
which is where I grew up on the East
Coast. Then, when I turned 20 years old,
I moved to California. Unfortunately,
because I did not have my cosmetology
license
long enough in Maryland when I moved to
California, I had to retake the
cosmetology
State Board exam. It was a very
stressful time, but I passed again.
When you are a hair stylist, you can
either specialize in hair cutting
or hair coloring, or you can do both.
When I worked in the salon, I had many
male clients. My male clients were very
regular with their haircuts. They would
see me every 3 to 4 weeks. I would like
to give you some tips on how to explain
to your hair stylist what kind of
hairstyle you would like or what kind of
haircut you would like. First of all,
please bring a picture of your ideal
haircut because your description
of your ideal haircut may translate
differently to the stylist. A lot of my
clients liked to have short on the
sides, short in the back, and longer at
the top so that they could sweep their
hair to the side or sweep it back.
This kind of hairstyle does require a
little bit of attention every day if you
would like to style it. If you naturally
have curly hair and you prefer it to be
smooth and wavy or straight, then you
have to blow dry it with a brush and a
hair dryer. There's a special brush that
I absolutely love to use. It's called a
Denman brush. It has a rubber base so
that the rubber can grab the hair easily
when you're blow drying and the bristles
are nice and sturdy. I would teach my
clients to hold the blow dryer in your
non-dominant
hand, which is the hand that you do not
write with, and hold the brush with your
dominant hand, which is the hand that
you do write with. Next, you would place
the brush on your head with the bristle
side down on the scalp and lift the hair
in this motion. So, you would do this
kind of
rainbow motion while the blow dryer is
drying it. So, you do this
simultaneously,
which is together. Then, once the hair
is fully dried, they would use a pomade
or a kind of sticky, thicker type of
cream to set the hairstyle in place and
make it look nice and polished. Some of
my male clients prefer to have a shorter
length on the top. So, short on the
sides, short in the back, and short on
the top. To style this, I recommend
taking a little bit of pomade, about a
dime size, placing it in the palm of
your hand. Then, you would rub your
palms together in a circular motion,
circular.
And then, you can do this.
This motion. So, you're taking the
product and you're rubbing it on the top
of your head lightly, also in a circular
motion. Then, all you have to do is use
your fingertips to add some dimension or
spike at the top, just lightly. That
hairstyle is very easy. I also had some
male clients who had long hair that they
like to put in a ponytail sometimes,
like this. Usually, the men that had the
long hair would not blow-dry their hair,
and they wouldn't style it. They would
just let their hair air-dry, which means
no blow-dryer, just natural air drying
it by itself. Another popular hairstyle
is a buzz cut. That means that you take
your trimmers and you put a guard on it
and you just glide it across your head,
or I would. I would glide it across
their head. I would taper the edges.
Taper means that it comes down to a
shorter length along the perimeter of
their hair. That way, when it grows out,
it grows out nice and naturally without
a harsh line here. The most difficult
hair to cut
with men
is the really stick-straight
hair.
Stick-straight is
a saying or a phrase that means that it
is as straight as a stick. Another
difficulty as a hair stylist is when
someone has a really strong cowlick.
Cowlick is the term where your hair does
a circle at the root of the scalp. Now,
onto women's haircuts. A lot of my
female clients had long hair, and a lot
of them liked to have face-framing
layers. This is a face-framing
layer. Can you guess why this is called
a face-framing
layer?
Because it frames
the face. There are many different
lengths of layers
you can cut into women's long hair.
I prefer longer or medium-length
layers. The length that I have right
now, I would consider to be called
medium-length.
So, when you go to your stylist, you
could say, "I would like to have
medium-length
hair."
Show them a photo so they understand
your definition of medium-length.
Some women like bobs. Bobs are shoulder
length hair, which looks like this.
When you blow dry your hair, it is
recommended to protect your hair from
the heat. I like using
a heat styling cream or a little bit of
a hair oil. I also like a volumizing
spray. It allows my hair to stay lifted
throughout the day instead of limp. I'm
